arabic: هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ
translation: “He named you ‘Muslims’ before, and in this Qur’an, so that the Messenger may be a witness over you, and that you may be witnesses over mankind.”

sunni.label: Sunni emphasis
sunni.body: Sunni tafsir reads the witnesses as the whole Muslim community — God’s chosen nation, which on Judgment Day testifies that the prophets delivered their message.

shia.label: Shia emphasis
shia.body: Shia tafsir reads the witnesses as the purified Imams of the Prophet’s Household — God’s witnesses over creation, a standing witness in every age.

voiceover.hook: This verse hands the believers a title — witnesses over mankind. But who does that mean?
voiceover.question: Which of these two readings resonates with you
